options.salts_anti_aliasing.dropdown.too: Current mode: %1$s. %2$s Click to show or hide the mode list.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.tooltip: Anti-aliasing is unavailable while Improved Transparency is on. Turn that option off to switch modes. Current mode: %1$s. %2$s
Anti-aliasing requires Minecraft's Vulkan graphics API. Set Graphics API to Vulkan and restart Minecraft. Current mode: %1$s. %2$s
%s is unavailable while Improved Transparency is on.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.off.sum: Disables anti-aliasing and upscaling. The independent Sharpness control can still be used, or left at 0% for an untouched vanilla image.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fxaa.su: Uses a fast post-process edge filter. Use it when you want a lightweight smoothness boost with very little setup. Benefit: low performance cost and broad compatibility.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.msaa.su: Samples polygon edges multiple times while keeping cutout textures binary by default. Optional alpha-to-coverage can smooth foliage edges at the cost of possible distant fading.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.ssaa.su: Renders the scene above native resolution and downsamples it. Use it when you want brute-force image quality and have plenty of performance headroom. Benefit: excellent edge cleanup and very stable detail.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.smaa.su: Detects edge patterns and blends along them more carefully than FXAA. Use it when you want stronger smoothing without as much softness. Benefit: cleaner diagonals and better detail retention.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.taa.sum: Blends current and previous frames to calm shimmering over time. Use it when thin detail flickers or distant edges crawl during motion. Benefit: the steadiest image on moving scenes and fine geometry.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.nis_ups: Renders below native resolution and scales the scene back up. Use the independent Sharpness control to choose how much detail enhancement is applied afterward.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.dlss_su: Reconstructs a native-resolution image with NVIDIA DLSS on supported RTX hardware using Vulkan. The Windows x64 release includes the required runtime automatically.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fsr2_su: Uses AMD FSR2 through the bundled native FidelityFX runtime on Vulkan to reconstruct a native-resolution image from a lower internal render resolution. Requires supported Vulkan hardware.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fsr3_su: Uses AMD FSR3 super resolution through the bundled native FidelityFX runtime without frame generation. Requires supported Vulkan hardware.
Uses AMD FSR3 super resolution plus the native FidelityFX frame-generation path. Requires a supported Vulkan frame-generation swapchain context.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.mode.fsr1_up: Renders below native resolution and reconstructs the image with edge-aware scaling. Use it when you want a balanced performance boost with cleaner edges than plain upscaling. Benefit: better detail reconstruction at lower internal resolutions.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.sharpness.to: Controls sharpening independently from the selected anti-aliasing or upscale mode. 0% disables sharpening; higher values add crispness but can create halos or crunchy detail when pushed too far.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.msaa_samples: Sets how many samples MSAA uses on polygon edges. Higher values smooth edges better but cost more GPU time. The renderer may fall back to your GPU's maximum supported sample count.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.msaa_alpha_t: Optionally converts cutout texture alpha into MSAA sample coverage. This can smooth the edges of leaves, vines, and grass, but may make distant cutouts fade or stipple. Off keeps Minecraft's binary cutout behavior.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa_scale.t: Sets the render scale on each axis before downsampling. 200% is conventional 4x SSAA, while 400% renders 16x as many scene pixels. The maximum is 800% per axis.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa_scale.w: Warning: %1$s renders %2$s as many scene pixels as native resolution. Values above 400% may heavily impact performance, use large amounts of GPU memory, or exceed your GPU's maximum texture size.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.upscale_qual: Chooses the internal render scale for NIS Upscale and FSR1 Upscale. Quality stays closer to native resolution, while lower presets trade image fidelity for more FPS.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.nis_upscale_: Controls the render scale for NIS Upscale. Higher presets stay sharper, while lower presets push performance harder. Use it when you want to fine-tune the balance between FPS and clarity.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.fsr1_upscale: Controls the render scale for FSR1 Upscale. Higher presets stay closer to native quality, while lower presets favor speed.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_quality: DLAA renders at native resolution for maximum detail. Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance progressively reduce the input resolution to improve FPS. Auto chooses a mode from the output resolution.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.dlss_: Auto uses perceptual SDR for vanilla's 8-bit target and linear/HDR processing for floating-point targets. Override only when your shader renderer uses a different encoding. Linear/HDR preserves a 16-bit floating-point scene; it does not enable HDR on your display or add shader-pack support by itself.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.motio: Maximum captured object vertices per frame. Larger budgets support more complex moving geometry and use more CPU/upload memory. The renderer reports skipped geometry when the budget is reached. Particle billboards are tracked separately.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.dlss_: Translucent particles supply their own velocity only above this opacity. Lower values improve tracking of faint particles but may give the background their motion. Higher values preserve background tracking. Opaque particle cutouts keep vanilla's alpha test.

Auto uses NVIDIA's runtime default for each quality mode. K, M and L request a specific transformer preset, including in DLAA. All support RTX GPUs; M and L cost more GPU time, especially on RTX 20/30 cards. NVIDIA App overrides can take precedence.
Chooses the FSR2/FSR3 temporal upscaling scale. Native AA keeps the scene at native resolution, while lower presets trade image fidelity for more FPS.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.config.toolti: Configure anti aliasing, upscaling and sharpening for the 3D scene. The HUD stays at native resolution.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.retry.toolti: Retry a failed rendering path at a safe frame boundary. Inspect the status above if the problem returns.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.reset_all.to: Restore defaults and select Off. Custom native runtime locations are preserved.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.native_runti: Optional overrides. Restart Minecraft after changing these values.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.fxaa_: Higher values smooth isolated pixel detail more, but can soften textures. Lower values preserve detail.
Lower values detect more edges and cost more filtering work. Higher values preserve more texture detail.
Minimum contrast needed to filter an edge. Lower values also smooth darker, low-contrast features.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.smaa_: Controls edge search length, diagonal search and corner handling. Ultra is most expensive.
Lower values detect more subtle edges. Too low may soften texture patterns.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.spati: Smooth the internal-resolution image before spatial reconstruction. Recommended for FSR1 and NIS. Off retains their original aliased input.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.ssaa_: Area integrates covered supersamples. Tent uses a wider, softer footprint to suppress fine-pattern aliasing.
Average light values rather than display-encoded values to avoid dark mixed pixels. Disable for the legacy color response.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_h: Higher values stabilize thin detail but can increase trails. Zero uses current-frame reconstruction only.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_l: Reject history when brightness changes. Higher values reduce trails but can increase flicker.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_d: Higher values reject more history across depth changes. Excessive rejection can destabilize silhouettes.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_v: Wider clipping preserves more history and detail, but can retain stale color. Lower values reject more aggressively.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_j: Number of distinct subpixel sample positions. More phases improve coverage but need more frames to converge.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.taa_h: Catmull-Rom preserves more detail; bilinear is cheaper and softer.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.entit: Account for moving entities during temporal reprojection. Shared by temporal methods. Disable for comparison or troubleshooting.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.react: Strength of additional history rejection for unexplained color changes, animated textures and moving surfaces. Shared by DLSS and FSR.
Lower values reject smaller color changes. Too low can interfere with subpixel accumulation.
Limit how strongly the extra color-change mask favors new samples. Zero disables this extra rejection.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.sharp: Adaptive Contrast limits sharpening near strong edges. Custom Unsharp provides a traditional filter. Both use the sharpening amount above.
Maximum added halo beyond the nearby color range. Zero suppresses overshoot; larger values allow stronger bright/dark outlines.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.frame: Generate intermediate frames using the supported FidelityFX swapchain. At least 60 rendered fps is recommended. Requires supported hardware and runtime.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.debug: Visualize an actual rendering signal for this method. These views replace scene color and are intended for troubleshooting.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.recor: Write frame timings and renderer events locally to the game logs folder. No data is uploaded.
Estimated color/depth payload of directly owned AA scene/history targets. Excludes transient pools, SDK allocations and driver overhead.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.mip_b: Optional terrain MIP bias for upscalers. Automatic follows the render/output ratio. More negative values retain detail but can increase shimmer or moire. Off keeps vanilla sampling.
Terrain texture LOD offset in quarter levels. Negative values retain finer detail; positive values soften texture aliasing.
Added to log2(render width / output width), with an extra -1 for temporal upscalers. Positive adjustments reduce aggressive fine-detail sampling.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.fsr_c: How strongly changing translucent composition rejects history. Higher values can reduce trails but destabilize fine detail.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.fsr_t: Minimum inferred translucent contribution change before marking composition as unstable.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.fsr_r: Scale of the transparency edge-change mask. Raise it for trails; lower it for more temporal accumulation.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.t: Select DLSS to configure it. Its setup button appears below Advanced controls. Rendering requires Vulkan, a supported RTX GPU and a configured runtime.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.in: DLSS is optional. Download NVIDIA Streamline %s, extract the archive, then connect its production runtime files. NVIDIA runtime DLLs are not included in this mod.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.pl: DLSS runtime import currently supports Windows x64. Other anti-aliasing methods remain available on supported renderers.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.in: Select nvngx_dlss.dll from the extracted bin/x64 folder, or choose that folder/the extracted SDK folder. All five matching runtime DLLs must be present.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.pi: Choose the downloaded files in the system window.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.ca: Selection cancelled. Your existing settings were kept.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.su: Files connected to this Minecraft instance. Restart Minecraft, then select DLSS Super Resolution in Anti Aliasing Settings. You can remove the original download folder.
screen.salts_anti_aliasing.dlss_setup.ov: A developer runtime override is active for this launch and takes precedence over the saved folder.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.upsca: Smooths first-person hand and item edges at native display resolution after upscaling. Higher sample counts use more GPU time and memory. Falls back to supported hardware limits.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.tuning.hand_: Uses multisample coverage for alpha-cutout hand and item materials, such as leaves. Blended materials retain their normal transparency.
